notes.title: Devlog 17.1: Bug fixes
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/dd3280ace7bdee41836ad2738035bb16b5ad60ac.png

Hello Everyone,

This build mainly focuses on fixing bugs found across various gameplay elements (Construction, placement, game -> server optimizations to name a few). This build doesn't bring new big features, instead it's all about smoothing gameplay. 

Have a look at everything that's changed:

 I decided to retire the Decorative logs and Turnips, the logs contribute to fluctuating frame rates and the turnips are losing their place in the game's natural ecosystem with every new build we publish. Unfortunately, the turnips have become too foreign to the rest of the game objects.
 Resized in-game chat section on the server settings page
 Saving inventory optimized to fix rare occasions where the latest inventory items are not saved when force-quitting
 Adjusted rain intervals and changed the rain color
 When you cast your hook into the water, the splash didn't always splash
 Fixed bug where all other player names were 'JMG' and their armor would be invisible
 Fixed a bug where whilst holding a bow and using the inventory, you would hear the bow cancel sound play
 When using any actions in the inventory, the items will now first be removed before the result is received (When you Clean a fish, instead of getting the fish fillets and then giving the fish, now you will give the fish and then get the fish fillets)
 Fixed a bug where on rare occasions the Hammer tool could be used to pick up anyone's construction parts, where you should only be able to use it to pick up your own construction parts
 There is now an 800ms limit before you can close your backpack from the time you opened it. This buffer exists to ensure the server and game finished syncing. 
 New Cheat: Teleport feature. This is currently restricted to server moderators who can find the correct info within the game server (through the Dev view hidden page). Soon this will be released so that you can teleport to others (or setpoints) that can be teleported to in creative mode or through a flag in the server settings.
 Wall Lights and Fires are now brighter
 "Door locked!" Notify when you try and open a door of which you don't have the key
 Fixed a bug where loading different worlds could leave the Creative mode and Instacraft toggles on the server out of sync
 The settings page is currently undergoing work so that we can introduce key-mapping. But for this build, we have disabled pages for input, sounds, graphics, and the survival guide as they are not ready.
 We tweaked how fish will battle when you try and fish them. You will have to subdue them a little more to reel them in
 Adjusted snapping construction parts, they should not interfere so easily with one another now
 Various minor system adjustments and internal simplifications bring a 10 - 20fps increase, depending on the system. This is to allow lower-end computers to enjoy the game.


Sadly there wasn't enough time to bring a new feature as well, but I felt that these fixes will make an immediate difference when you play. So enjoy them whilst I work on the next best idea. In the mean time, thank you for following Era, thank you for your time and thank you for the support :)

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Small Update: Save your World
notes.notes:
Hello Everyone,

Just a small update to bring about some big change in gameplay. This build enables a move away from "playing offline" to "Single Player", we also fixed an issue with the player's belt and fixed a placement bug.

Load and save
Players can now create a new world through the Single Player option in the main menu. You name your world. Your world will autosave every 10 minutes, or you can save in the in-game settings menu or when going to the main menu. Players can create as many worlds as they like.

Issue with belt
There was an issue where the tools and weapons you have in your belt (the 5 slot strip at the bottom of the screen) would disappear when you exit and enter the game. This has been fixed. 

Placement bug
A bug was present whereupon equipping a placeable item like a storage box, fireplace, or even a wall, initially placement would be denied by highlighting the object in red. Swopping between slots seems to have been a quick fix. This has been rectified. Object placement collision will now respond appropriately.

Forever Pitch dark bug
We picked up a while ago that a handful of players were met with a completely pitch black landscape when starting a game playing offline. As if time was not moving and it was constant night. We managed to replicate the issue and it seemed to have been from older graphics hardware and their compatible shader model, however as German user Chaoshexe communicated his experience to us, it became clear that this was related to the fact that Windows would have different regional settings set on his computer. 
After investigation, we found that this graphical issue is because of his decimal separator, being a comma. In some countries, a comma is used as a decimal separator. In other countries, a dot is used. What happened is that time would be synced as a decimal, and between the game and the server there was confusion over the comma. So we have now learned and fixed - Thank you for your input, Chaoshexe!


We are currently knee-deep with Devlog 15, but we felt that the ability to load and save a world would give players the opportunity to turn their houses into the palaces they want. The bugs addressed also weighed heavily on the urgency. We want our players to have a stable gameplay experience, not a frustrating one where constant hiccups ruin the immersion. 

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 11: New sounds, server enhancements, bug fixes and rain
notes.notes:
Hello Everyone,

With this update we bring you the first element of our plan to incorporate weather and temperature into Era of Survival. We also added new sounds that makes gameplay more fun, we made adjustments to our server to speed things up and we got a few reported bugs out as well. Sadly we are not ready yet with body armor. Let's have a look:

Notable changes

 New In-Game Settings menu
We cleaned up the settings menu a little. From here it's much easier to add more settings for players to change.
We also fixed a bug where if you had the backpack and camp fire open, then the settings page would show and the camp fire dialog will be over it..
 New Sounds
We added a few new sounds to make the game more engaging:
Tree fall over and crash sound
Wolf death sound
Sound of rain at different intensities
Sound of wind blowing
 Fixed stairs placement issue
Some players could not place stairs properly on foundations, which prevented them from building multi-storey houses. You can now place your stairs on the foundation - as of this update, you can now rotate the stairs too
 You could open a storage box from 10 metres away
Very handy, but not within arms length.. So we adjusted this to a more proper distance
 Rare count issue when drag and drop and combining items between the backpack and the storage box
Here you would drag and drop wood together and if it's more than 200 (Maximum Stack Size) then you will get 200 + (insert wrong amount here). Remember that if you combine items in the inventory, if you add up above the 200 limit per slot, the difference will be added in a new slot, chosen from the first open or same slot by looking from the first one
 Change in speed for the dams
Our dams were moving a little fast, more like streams down a river. Now they move more like a dam
 Change in Notifications
When your inventory is full or your tool breaks, you will get a notification now.
 Camp Fires cook inconsistently
We noticed that when players leave food in the fire, sometimes you would check after being away for a while, and even though the fire was on the whole time, it did not use any wood and did not cook any food. You can now safely trust your fire and leave it unattended to cook without supervision
 Avatar holding tools
We noticed that the avatar was not holding certain tools properly. This has been corrected, but we intend on returning to this.
 Startup tips pop up every time the game starts
We put these tips in at startup to help new players find their bearings in a matter of minutes. This was successful and indeed helpful. But after a while they become more intrusive than helpful. So now they will only show up in the first 10 starts, then it will stop showing up. When we send a game update, they will reset and start showing again for 10 times.
 We made it rain
The grass is that green for a reason. This particular piece of land you now call home, has a very good rain fall around this time of year. Every couple of minutes the weather will change and (across the server) it will rain outside. Soon enough you will get cold if you stay outside and you would hide from the rain inside your warm house.


That's it for now. We hope these changes and additions will help our players enjoy the best of Era of Survival. We stay committed to our project and those who have supported us - to continue expanding and improving our game. 

Until next time,

Cheers
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 09: Enhancements and bug fixes
notes.notes:
Hello Everyone,

For this week we worked to improve current systems all over the game as well as fix a few bugs along the way. We also looked at making some tasks in the game a little simpler, like drag and drop in the inventory, easier object placement and tweaks to tool durability and tool efficiencies. 

Notables:

 New features for your backpack
You can now drag and drop your supplies around to any slot you want. You can also drop similar supplies together to combine them together. Remember that your backpack has only 15 slots available. A small storage box has 10, and a large storage box has 20.
 Bug: Spinach not growing at the farm
When you planted spinach at the farm base, your progress would increase and your plot will still dry, but nothing would grow, in fact the plant type was nothing too. This is now fixed. Enjoy juicy spinach :)
 Enhancements to the object placement system
Players will notice a few differences when they put objects down now. When you hold something you can place down, like a camp fire, your character will now get out of the way so you can have a full view and put the object down. The object's placeholder will also now be where your red dot marker is aiming. Wall lights will also now face you when you put them down. They are no longer bound to only always inside lights.
 Tips on the loading screen
While you wait for the game to load when you log in to the server, you will now see handy tips that will help you survive better. Once the game is done loading, a button will appear that reads 'Play'. Click it to continue.
 New sound at the dams
Dams are a little more pleasant now, you can hear moving water and a few birds. Perfect for a sunset-by-the-dam house
 Internal tools upgrade
We mention this one to help assure our supporters that we are only interested in bringing something better to the table. Players that have used all of the available tools in game thus far, might have noticed that in very rare circumstances, some tools didn't react when used on some objects. Seeing that we have an ever growing amount of new objects, as well as a few more new tools on the roadmap, and a very primitive (Excel) way of keeping track of how objects and tools react, we had to take a minute and brainstorm on a better solution, then develop it. Now we are better equipped, and can deploy new objects and tools in game much faster, leaving more time (and brainpower) to drill hard and solve bitchy bugs.
 Bug: NPC characters passing through structures and rocks
NPCs like wolves would sometimes pursue you through any obstacle, except a high hill.. Through the rocks, through walls.. This has been fixed.
 When opening your menu, your character would keep breathing and breathing heavily. He will now stop to match the fact that he is standing still



There are also minor bug fixes that we fixed whilst making all these changes. While we spend a fair amount of time on testing (versus development, marketing etc), we still prepare ourselves for new reported bugs. Sometimes you fix one thing, and it breaks something small elsewhere down the line of a completely different system. Next week is our 10th update to the game, and we want this to be a clear sign to our supporters that we remain dedicated. Even during the corona virus pandemic, our team members still work permanent jobs, but still make the time available to bring something better to the table. We remain committed to our cause, and have a long roadmap still to follow. 

Cheers for now,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 7.5: Small update
notes.notes:
Hello Everyone,

We have a few fixes ready but we really wanted players to have them available for the weekend. We will however still post a normal update on Sunday.

Notables:

 Fixed lock mouse to screen
For players with dual monitor setups, when playing, your mouse cursor will not leave the game unless you open your inventory or open settings.
 Improved character movement on server
A slight improvement on players syncing to the server that mainly involves rotation. Improves movement of other players on the online server.
 Issues with In-Game Chat
For some players in game chat was completely disabled. This should rectify the issue
 Corn stalk scale
This size is more relative to the sizes of other objects in the world.


There's been a few other minor improvements between systems in the game. One of our priorities is optimizing the game so that we can bring down the minimum hardware requirements as well as data usage over the internet. This will essentially help players with lower spec computers to join the game and play along.

Cheers for now!
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 07: Bug Fixes
notes.notes:
Hello Everyone,

For this week we looked at fixing a few common bugs and made improvements as well, but we mainly focused to complete upgrading Era's files to Unity 2019. This will be a less noticeable update, but rest assured that foundations were laid in the process of upgrading. Without further ado:

Gap exploits around houses 
To the dismay of some player on the online server, others have figured out that (with great precision) you can actually reach a fireplace inside the house if it was placed very close to the wall on the inside, even though you are on the outside. This has been fixed

Harvesting from a dead body
Similarly to above, when you harvest human meat from a dead body, if you hit at a weird angle, you can get an infinite supply of human meat

In game chat flickering
In game chat update timers caused a quick disappear and then reappear act which was really annoying and distracting, no matter how infrequent it happens. Its fixed.

Server optimisation
Our server provides data in layers to the game while you play, one of these layers (that dictates further away objects) wasn't working, which made a tree from far away stay standing when a player chops it down, and then the tree will finally disappear when you get close enough, which quite frankly, with the fog, gave it a sort of fog of war effect, but got fixed.

Black screen on start bug
Sometimes when logging into the game, you would get stuck on the "Loading" screen forever - relogging in fixes it, but what happened is that there was data loss when transmitting the creation of your player on the server. We suspect this was due to packet loss, because the feedback we got showed that this was also happening with the creation of tools and weapons. Just very intermittently and when playing offline, very very rarely. But we've isolated where this happens and put measures in place to recover when there was an issue.

Avatar only runs, cant walk anymore
Some players reported that their player can't walk, just idle or run. This was an interesting side effect that we might consider as something you can toggle in future, but we reverted back to walking for now.
Some players also told us that their avatars just kept running or walking when the menu got opened, even though the avatar was standing at the same place. Also been fixed.

Water well placement and sound
Waterwells will now no longer just spawn randomly. Instead they are now confined to groves, where they could even come in pairs or more. This is one step closer out the door for the water wells though. We are looking into alternatives that can offer the same to the player, but would appear naturally in the environment. We also fixed the sound

Cup durability
Lastly, your cup will now be able to serve you for much longer. Even though the cup was relatively cheap to make, it was still a hassle to wait 30 seconds for it to craft. So now it has increased durability.

We want to say thank you to our community without whom nothing would have been possible. We say thank you for your support. We also welcome our newcomers and as a developer, I implore current players to teach each other to play first, before just slicing and dicing one another.

As a team we stay committed to move forward with Era of Survival and with our roadmap, we hope to bring many new elements for the community to enjoy together.

Until next time,

Cheers!
Jean

notes.title: Quick update - performance and more
notes.notes:
Hello everyone :),

Due to the nature of the game, we understand that regular (perhaps too regular) updates can really ruin things for players playing online for a few hours when the server needs to be updated (and your map wiped), however we had to finish work on performance issues that weren't yet ready with yesterdays update. 

We noted fps spikes and found that the issue is related to the dam placed on the map for water, for the moment we have changed the water to something that doesn't cause such lag spikes. We will polish the water up again, after we get it to stop causing such lag.

We also use this opportunity to then add a feature so you can respawn from the death screen to any of your beds. 

We also added some decor by the dam, let us know what you think.
